items.title: Court Ruling: Part Of Taxonomy Criteria Found Unlawful – But Polluting Planes And Ships Still Slipping Through The Net
items.original_title: Court Ruling: Part Of Taxonomy Criteria Found Unlawful – But Polluting Planes And Ships Still Slipping Through The Net
items.summary: Yesterday, the General Court in Luxembourg has published its judgment on the EU Commission’s Taxonomy Regulations on ‘green’ investments for aviation and shipping. We welcome the Court’s finding that part of the shipping taxonomy criteria is unlawful. “We welcome the Court’s finding that part of the shipping Taxonomy criteria is unlawful, risking letting LNG-powered ships producing significant quantities of the super-pollutant methane be considered ‘green’ investments. However, the fact that methane slippage must now be quantified still gives the green light to label an entirely new fleet of cruise ships and airplanes as green, even though they will be fossil-fuelled for another 30 years. This means that EU climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra needs to ask himself: does he truly believe that it is a sustainable choice to invest in new fossil-fuelled cruise ships and aircrafts?” “We urge Wopke Hoekstra to follow up on his speech on doubling down on climate action after all the extreme weather events this summer, and reconsider the Taxonomy so it fulfils its intended purpose: drive the green transition through financial flows.” In August 2024, a coalition of NGOs took the EU Commission to court over its decision to include high-emitting fossil fuel planes and ships in the EU’s flagship sustainable finance legislation, the EU Taxonomy.

items.title: UBS says iron ore consensus is too low: What it means for BHP, RIO and FMG
items.original_title: UBS says iron ore consensus is too low: What it means for BHP, RIO and FMG
items.summary: Analysts have been bearish on iron ore for years, and the forecasts keep calling for lower prices. But prices have held up better than most expected, and UBS thinks the consensus view is too narrow. “We believe consensus underestimates the durability of steel demand outside China, overstates future iron-unit supply growth by focusing on ore tonnes rather than contained iron units, and assumes greater cost curve flexibility than industry data supports,” said UBS in a 29 September note. UBS’ three reasons for higher long term iron ore price UBS says the market is underestimating the forces shaping iron ore over the next decade. Blast furnaces, which use iron ore, are running near 90% capacity, and UBS says scrap is supplementing iron ore rather than replacing it, concluding that “Chinese iron ore demand is more resilient than domestic property demand would suggest.” #2 Global South drives strong steel demand and offsets China retreat The second reason UBS gives is the rise of what it calls the “Global South”, a group of 14 developing countries including India, Indonesia, Vietnam, Brazil and Saudi Arabia, with a combined population of about 2.9 billion.

items.title: Samsung Heavy Wins Order for Two Large Gas Carriers Worth 307.4 Billion Won
items.original_title: Samsung Heavy Wins Order for Two Large Gas Carriers Worth 307.4 Billion Won
items.summary: Samsung Heavy Industries (010140) said on the 30th that it has won an order for two very large gas carriers from a shipowner based in Bermuda. The contract is valued at 307.4 billion won ($221 million). The vessels are scheduled to be delivered to the customer by February 2030. In its commercial shipbuilding division, Samsung Heavy Industries secured contracts for 16 vessels in the second half of this year, following 28 in the first half. The company’s commercial ship orders this year total 44 vessels worth $7.5 billion (about 10.1497 trillion won), reaching 132% of its annual target of $5.7 billion (about 7.7138 trillion won). By vessel type, LNG carriers were the largest category at 18 ships, including one floating storage and regasification unit, followed by 14 crude oil tankers, six gas carriers, four container ships and two ethane carriers. In its offshore division, the company won orders for two floating LNG production facilities worth $4.4 billion (about 5.954 trillion won). Combined shipbuilding and offshore orders came to 46 vessels worth $11.9 billion (about 16.1137 trillion won), or 86% of the company’s annual order target of $13.9 billion (about 18.8219 trillion won).

items.original_title: Eastern Pacific takes delivery of LNG-capable dual fuel car carrier
items.summary: Singapore-based shipowner Eastern Pacific Shipping (EPS) has taken delivery of a new LNG dual-fuel pure car and truck carrier (PCTC) that Spain’s Suardiaz Group will operate under a charter. The 5,500 CEU vessel RS Atlantico was built at the Xiamen shipyard which is a part of China’s Fujian Chuanzheng Shipbuilding group. The vessel was developed as a collaboration between EPS and Suardiaz. The vessel has left the shipyard for Europe, Suardiaz said. During the launch of the vessel in June, Suardiaz said it will operate on the company’s Atlantic routes. It is the first PCTC newbuilding EPS has chartered to Suardiaz, and the first LNG dual-fuel PCTC to join Suardiaz’s operations. Source: By Nachiket Tekawade, ENGINE, https://www.engine.online/news/

items.title: EU’s need to raise steel output requires millions of tons of extra scrap: think tank
items.original_title: EU’s need to raise steel output requires millions of tons of extra scrap: think tank
items.summary: The EU must boost crude steel production 12%-13% by 2027 to counter falling imports triggered by steel safeguards and the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, but meeting this target and rolling out new electric arc furnaces will require an additional 8 million-11 million metric tons of steel scrap later this decade, Stanislav Zinchenko, CEO of Kyiv-based think tank GMK Center, told Platts, part of S&P Global Energy. The EU was importing 7 million mt/year of long rolled steel before, with half of that tonnage produced via the blast furnace-basic oxygen furnace steelmaking route. Now, because of the safeguards and CBAM, this volume is likely to be replaced by EU-based scrap-intensive EAF production, he said. To replace the expected decline in steel imports, the required 12%-13% growth by 2027 in EU crude steel production, from 2025 levels, will need an extra 4 million-6 million mt of steel scrap. Then, by 2028, the commissioning of new EAFs could further boost domestic scrap demand by 4 million-5 million mt, according to Zinchenko.

items.title: GAO Finds Marine Firefighting Gaps Persist at U.S. Ports
items.original_title: GAO Finds Marine Firefighting Gaps Persist at U.S. Ports
items.summary: The Coast Guard, Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, Newark Fire Department, and multiple state and area agencies respond to a fire in Port Newark on the vehicle carrier ship, Grande Costa D’Avorio. Fire fighting crews are working to extinguish the fire both from the pier and from FDNY fireboats. (U.S. Coast Guard photo by Dan Henry) A new federal watchdog report says gaps in training, coordination and emergency planning continue to complicate the response to ship fires at U.S. The Government Accountability Office report found 886 nearshore marine fires were reported to the U.S. gCaptain covered the firefighting response at the time . The Coast Guard established a National Salvage and Marine Firefighting Task Force in January 2024 and has since developed online training and other tools. GAO said Coast Guard officials and marine firefighting providers described a broader “wait and see” problem in which vessel operators may hesitate to activate response plans because of the expense associated with mobilizing commercial firefighting and salvage resources. The watchdog also issued five recommendations to the Coast Guard, including assigning marine firefighting coordination duties to specific field personnel, working with local fire departments to arrange vessel tours and exercises, creating a system for sharing lessons and best practices, and providing clearer guidance on when vessel response plans should be activated.
